svg.font-family: 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace

metadata.orrery:spec:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=../references/diagram.schema.json title: OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with PKCE subtitle: "RFC 7636: the app proves at the token endpoint that it started the login, so a stolen code is useless" kind: sequence
# Left to right in the order they first take part: the user's browser starts it. nodes: browser: { icon: generic:browser, label: Browser } app: { icon: generic:server, label: Web app, note: OAuth client } auth: { icon: generic:auth, label: Authorization server } api: { icon: generic:api, label: Resource API }
# Top to bottom is time: calls solid, answers dashed back to the caller. edges: - browser -> app: GET /login - app -> app: "new code_verifier, S256 code_challenge" - app --> browser: "302 to /authorize (code_challenge, state)" - browser -> auth: "GET /authorize (client_id, code_challenge)" - auth --> browser: sign-in and consent page - browser -> auth: "POST credentials, approve scopes" - auth --> browser: "302 to /callback (code, state)" - browser -> app: "GET /callback (code, state)" - app -> auth: "POST /token (code, code_verifier)" - auth -> auth: "SHA-256(code_verifier) = code_challenge?" - auth --> app: access and refresh tokens - auth --> app: "400 invalid_grant" - app -> api: "GET /me (Bearer access token)" - api --> app: 200 profile - app --> browser: session cookie, home page
# The token endpoint answers one of two ways; only a matching verifier gets tokens. fragments: - type: alt label: verifier matches from: 11 to: 12 else: [{ at: 12, label: no match }]

svg.title: OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with PKCE
svg.desc: OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with PKCE. Sequence diagram with 4 participants (Browser, Web app, Authorization server, Resource API) and 15 messages. 1. Browser to Web app (GET /login); 2. Web app to itself (new code_verifier, S256 code_challenge); 3. Web app to Browser (302 to /authorize (code_challenge, state)); 4. Browser to Authorization server (GET /authorize (client_id, code_challenge)); 5. Authorization server to Browser (sign-in and consent page); 6. Browser to Authorization server (POST credentials, approve scopes); 7. Authorization server to Browser (302 to /callback (code, state)); 8. Browser to Web app (GET /callback (code, state)); 9. Web app to Authorization server (POST /token (code, code_verifier)); 10. Authorization server to itself (SHA-256(code_verifier) = code_challenge?); 11. Authorization server to Web app (access and refresh tokens); 12. Authorization server to Web app (400 invalid_grant); 13. Web app to Resource API (GET /me (Bearer access token)); 14. Resource API to Web app (200 profile); 15. Web app to Browser (session cookie, home page). Fragments: alt [verifier matches] over messages 11 to 12, else [no match] from 12.

text.tspan: OAUTH 2.0 AUTHORIZATION CODE FLOW WITH PKCE
RFC 7636: the app proves at the token endpoint that it started the login, so a stolen code is useless
